02-08.title: Spanish Civil War : Republican forces establish the Interprovincial Council of Santander, Palencia and Burgos in Cantabria .

02-28.title: The final episode of M*A*S*H airs, with almost 110 million viewers.

12-07.title: In Texas, Charles Brooks Jr., becomes the first person to be executed by lethal injection in the United States.

09-29.title: Calder Hall, the world's first commercial nuclear power station, is demolished in a controlled explosion.

09-03.title: North Korea conducts its sixth and most powerful nuclear test .

09-27.title: USAF Captain Milburn G. Apt becomes the first person to exceed Mach 3. Shortly thereafter, the Bell X-2 goes out of control and Captain Apt is killed.

01-04.title: Constantine Hangerli arrives in Bucharest, Wallachia, as its new Prince, invested by the Ottoman Empire .

01-03.title: Proceedings of the U.S. Congress are televised for the first time.

04-03.title: Jack the Ripper : The first of 11 unsolved brutal murders of women committed in or near the impoverished Whitechapel district in the East End of London, occurs.

12-15.title: The town of Ekenäs ( Finnish : Tammisaari ) is founded by King Gustav Vasa of Sweden .

10-08.title: Yom Kippur War : Israel loses more than 150 tanks in a failed attack on Egyptian-occupied positions.

09-09.title: The citizens of Lisbon celebrate the triumphal return of the explorer Vasco de Gama, completing his two-year journey around the Cape of Good Hope to India.

09-17.title: Flanders Campaign : France completes its conquest of the Austrian Netherlands at the Battle of Sprimont .

02-21.title: In New York City, Edwin Land demonstrates the first " instant camera ", the Polaroid Land Camera, to a meeting of the Optical Society of America .

11-14.title: The Congress of Colombia, in commemoration of the 150th anniversary of the death of Policarpa Salavarrieta, declares this day as "Day of the Colombian Woman".

02-20.title: An earthquake cracks open the Sinila volcanic crater on the Dieng Plateau, releasing poisonous H 2 S gas and killing 149 villagers in the Indonesian province of Central Java .

05-10.title: Vietnam War : The Battle of Dong Ap Bia begins with an assault on Hill 937. It will ultimately become known as Hamburger Hill .

05-14.title: Ten people are killed in a mass shooting in Buffalo, New York .

03-05.title: Boston Massacre : Five Americans, including Crispus Attucks, are fatally shot by British troops in an event that would contribute to the outbreak of the American Revolutionary War (also known as the American War of Independence) five years later.

04-21.title: The city of Rattanakosin, now known internationally as Bangkok, is founded on the eastern bank of the Chao Phraya River by King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke .

05-07.title: Indochina War : The Battle of Dien Bien Phu ends in a French defeat and a Viet Minh victory (the battle began on March 13).

05-21.title: The Order of St. Alexander Nevsky is instituted in Russia by Empress Catherine I . It would later be discontinued and then reinstated by the Soviet government in 1942 as the Order of Alexander Nevsky .

12-09.title: Gabriel Narutowicz is elected the first president of Poland.

01-16.title: The Mali War begins when Tuareg militias start fighting the Malian government for independence.

11-04.title: The United States government establishes the National Security Agency, or NSA.

01-23.title: The episcopal seat is moved from Nousiainen to Koroinen (located near the current centre of Turku ) by the permission of Pope Gregory IX . The date is starting to be considered as the founding of Turku.

02-15.title: The decimalisation of the currencies of the United Kingdom and Ireland is completed on Decimal Day .

11-21.title: Thomas Edison announces his invention of the phonograph, a machine that can record and play sound.

09-13.title: The IBM 305 RAMAC is introduced, the first commercial computer to use disk storage .

05-04.title: Nine people are killed and thirteen injured in a spree shooting in Mladenovac and Smederevo, Serbia . It is the second mass shooting in the country in two days.

03-08.title: The Safavid Empire of Iran is defeated by an army from Afghanistan at the Battle of Gulnabad .

01-17.title: Mexican War of Independence : In the Battle of Calderón Bridge, a heavily outnumbered Spanish force of 6,000 troops defeats nearly 100,000 Mexican revolutionaries.

12-30.title: Proposed budget cuts by Benjamin Netanyahu spark protests from 250,000 workers who shut down services across Israel.

10-05.title: An Indonesian Air Force C-130 crash kills 135 people.

02-05.title: The New Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg, Russia, one of the largest and oldest museums in the world, opens to the public.

01-31.title: Finnish Civil War : The Suinula massacre, which changes the nature of the war in a more hostile direction, takes place in Kangasala .

06-07.title: Sette Giugno : Nationalist riots break out in Valletta, the capital of Malta . British soldiers fire into the crowd, killing four people.

11-23.title: The Cocos Islands are transferred from the control of the United Kingdom to that of Australia.

02-19.title: Transfer of Crimea : The Soviet Politburo of the Soviet Union orders the transfer of the Crimean Oblast from the Russian SFSR to the Ukrainian SSR .

09-23.title: Pope Callixtus II and Holy Roman Emperor Henry V agree to the Concordat of Worms to put an end to the Investiture Controversy .

11-20.title: In England, a fire breaks out in Windsor Castle, badly damaging the castle and causing over £50 million worth of damage.

06-01.title: European Central Bank is founded in Brussels .

02-10.title: World War II : Attempting to completely lift the Siege of Leningrad, the Soviet Red Army engages German troops and Spanish volunteers in the Battle of Krasny Bor .

10-25.title: World War II: The final attempt of the Imperial Japanese Navy to win the war climaxes at the Battle of Leyte Gulf .

11-25.title: Românul de la Pind, the longest-running newspaper by and about Aromanians until World War II, ceases its publications.

06-04.title: Italian Independence wars : In the Battle of Magenta, the French army, under Louis-Napoleon, defeat the Austrian army.

11-15.title: The world population reached eight billion .

02-09.title: The Beatles make their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show, performing before a record-setting audience of 73 million viewers across the United States.

03-28.title: Brazilian high school student Edson Luís de Lima Souto is killed by military police at a student protest.

06-06.title: Battle of Novara . In the Italian Wars, Swiss troops defeat the French under Louis II de la Trémoille, forcing them to abandon Milan ; Duke Massimiliano Sforza is restored.

05-23.title: Cold War: The Western occupying powers approve the Basic Law and establish a new German state, the Federal Republic of Germany .

10-22.title: The male line of the Portuguese House of Burgundy becomes extinct with the death of King Fernando, leaving only his daughter Beatrice. Rival claimants begin a period of civil war and disorder.

10-31.title: Nevada is admitted as the 36th U.S. state .

08-12.title: South Africa is banned from the Olympic Games due to the country's racist policies .

08-21.title: NASA loses contact with the Mars Observer spacecraft.

01-07.title: Roger Lafontant, former leader of the Tonton Macoute in Haiti under François Duvalier, attempts a coup d'état, which ends in his arrest.

04-06.title: Vietnam War : Easter Offensive : American forces begin sustained air strikes and naval bombardments.

10-16.title: Leonid Brezhnev becomes leader of the Soviet Communist Party, while Alexei Kosygin becomes the head of government.

11-18.title: A fire occurs on a train traveling through the Channel Tunnel from France to England causing several injuries and damaging approximately 500 metres (1,600 ft) of tunnel.

09-28.title: World War II: Soviet Army troops liberate Klooga concentration camp in Estonia.

03-18.title: Flanders Campaign of the French Revolution, Battle of Neerwinden .

03-10.title: After establishing the city of Santo Domingo, Christopher Columbus departs for Spain, leaving his brother in command.

12-02.title: Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-27, a classified mission for the United States Department of Defense .

08-30.title: The Second Vienna Award reassigns the territory of Northern Transylvania from Romania to Hungary.

08-27.title: Eruption of Krakatoa : Four enormous explosions almost completely destroy the island of Krakatoa and cause years of climate change.

10-15.title: American Civil War: The Union garrison of Glasgow, Missouri surrenders to Confederate forces.

02-07.title: Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles leaves Singapore after just taking it over, leaving it in the hands of William Farquhar .

04-19.title: With no living male heirs, Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor, issues the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 to ensure that Habsburg lands and the Austrian throne would be inheritable by a female; his daughter and successor, Maria Theresa, was not born until 1717.

11-05.title: The three-day anti-Jewish riots in Tripolitania commence.

04-05.title: During the Battle on the Ice of Lake Peipus, Russian forces, led by Alexander Nevsky, rebuff an invasion attempt by the Teutonic Knights .

10-17.title: FLQ terrorists murder Quebec Vice-Premier and Minister of Labour Pierre Laporte.

08-06.title: Britain imposes the Lagos Treaty of Cession to suppress slavery in what is now Nigeria.

11-27.title: In Romania, the ruling Iron Guard fascist party assassinates over 60 of arrested King Carol II of Romania 's aides and other political dissidents.

01-19.title: The first electric lighting system employing overhead wires, built by Thomas Edison, begins service at Roselle, New Jersey .

09-16.title: The General Motors Corporation is founded.

11-03.title: George II of Greece regains his throne through a popular, though possibly fixed, plebiscite .

02-27.title: Gulf War : U.S. President George H. W. Bush announces that " Kuwait is liberated".

06-12.title: India, Judge Jagmohanlal Sinha of the city of Allahabad ruled that India's Prime Minister Indira Gandhi had used corrupt practices to win her seat in the Indian Parliament, and that she should be banned from holding any public office. Mrs. Gandhi sent word that she refused to resign.

12-19.title: Irish-born physician John Bodkin Adams is arrested in connection with the suspicious deaths of more than 160 patients. Eventually he is convicted only of minor charges.

08-09.title: Voepass Linhas Aéreas Flight 2283 crashes near Vinhedo, São Paulo, killing all 62 people on board.

04-24.title: The first segment of the Imperial Wireless Chain providing wireless telegraphy between Leafield in Oxfordshire, England, and Cairo, Egypt, comes into operation.

10-12.title: The city of Manizales, Colombia, is founded by 'The Expedition of the 20'.

10-19.title: American Civil War: Confederate agents based in Canada rob three banks in Saint Albans, Vermont.

12-21.title: Battle of Curalaba : The revolting Mapuche, led by cacique Pelentaru, inflict a major defeat on Spanish troops in southern Chile .

04-10.title: American Civil War : A day after his surrender to Union forces, Confederate General Robert E. Lee addresses his troops for the last time.

05-16.title: The 16 May 1877 crisis occurs in France, ending with the dissolution of the National Assembly 22 June and affirming the interpretation of the Constitution of 1875 as a parliamentary rather than presidential system . The elections held in October 1877 led to the defeat of the royalists as a formal political movement in France.

03-21.title: Annulment of the marriage of King Louis VII of France and Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine .

05-18.title: United States presidential election : Joe Biden announces his presidential campaign .

11-24.title: Conrad of Montferrat becomes King of Jerusalem upon his marriage to Isabella I of Jerusalem .

11-19.title: The second Canadian railway line, the Montreal and Lachine Railroad, is opened.

08-05.title: World War II: At least 1,104 Japanese POWs in Australia attempt to escape from a camp at Cowra, New South Wales ; 545 temporarily succeed but are later either killed, commit suicide, or are recaptured.

01-30.title: The Truce of Andrusovo is signed, ending the Russian-Polish War of 1654-1667

03-06.title: The town of Kajaani, known at the time as Cajanaburg, is founded by Count Per Brahe, the Governor-General of Finland .

06-09.title: Five hundred Mormons leave Iowa City, Iowa for the Mormon Trail .

03-02.title: Researchers at Fermilab announce the discovery of the top quark .

09-12.title: Austro-Ottoman War : Battle of Vienna : Several European armies join forces to defeat the Ottoman Empire .

06-11.title: Lombard Revolt : Greek citizens of Bari rise up against the Lombard rebels led by Melus and deliver the city to Basil Mesardonites, Byzantine governor ( catepan ) of the Catepanate of Italy .

04-29.title: World War II: Airdrops of food begin over German-occupied regions of the Netherlands.

12-05.title: World War II: Great Britain declares war on Finland, Hungary and Romania .

01-13.title: Coup d'état in Togo results in the assassination of president Sylvanus Olympio .

03-23.title: The Trần dynasty of Vietnam is deposed, after one hundred and seventy-five years of rule, by Hồ Quý Ly, a court official.

01-29.title: War of the Sixth Coalition : France defeats Russia and Prussia in the Battle of Brienne .

02-04.title: The city of Macapá in Brazil is founded by Sebastião Veiga Cabral.

12-13.title: Second Sino-Japanese War : Battle of Nanking : The city of Nanjing, defended by the National Revolutionary Army under the command of General Tang Shengzhi, falls to the Japanese . This is followed by the Nanking Massacre, in which Japanese troops rape and slaughter hundreds of thousands of civilians.

04-22.title: The 1st Air Commando Group using Sikorsky R-4 helicopters stage the first use of helicopters in combat with combat search and rescue operations in the China Burma India Theater .

07-27.title: The Jesuit priest Francis Xavier 's ship reaches Japan.

07-29.title: Astronomers announce their discovery of the dwarf planet Eris .

01-14.title: Roald Amundsen 's South Pole expedition makes landfall on the eastern edge of the Ross Ice Shelf .

03-20.title: The Republican Party of the United States is organized in Ripon, Wisconsin, US.

01-21.title: A B-52 bomber crashes near Thule Air Base, contaminating the area after its nuclear payload ruptures. One of the four bombs remains unaccounted for after the cleanup operation is complete.

05-31.title: A shooting occurs inside a municipal building at Virginia Beach, Virginia, leaving 13 people dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.

04-23.title: Blair Peach, a British activist, was fatally injured after being knocked unconscious during an Anti-Nazi League demonstration against a National Front election meeting in Southall, London.

03-01.title: Villarrica Volcano begins a strombolian eruption causing lahars that destroy half of the town of Coñaripe .

01-08.title: Turkish Airlines Flight 634 crashes near Diyarbakır Airport, Turkey, killing the entire crew and 70 of the 75 passengers.

08-18.title: Soviet-Japanese War : Battle of Shumshu : Soviet forces land at Takeda Beach on Shumshu Island and launch the Battle of Shumshu ; the Soviet Union ’s Invasion of the Kuril Islands commences.

09-06.title: India retaliates following Pakistan's Operation Grand Slam which results in the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 that ends in a stalemate followed by the signing of the Tashkent Declaration .

04-30.title: Eighty Years' War : Dutch Republic forces recapture a strategically important fort from Spain after a nine-month siege .

10-21.title: In the 1945 French legislative election French women vote for the first time.

10-27.title: Philadelphia is founded in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

08-24.title: Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly across the United States non-stop (from Los Angeles to Newark, New Jersey ).

08-14.title: The first sighting of the Falkland Islands by John Davis .

02-18.title: With Italian unification almost complete, Victor Emmanuel II of Piedmont, Savoy and Sardinia assumes the title of King of Italy .

04-17.title: Harald III of Denmark dies and is succeeded by Canute IV, who would later be the first Dane to be canonized .

03-13.title: Breonna Taylor is killed by police officers who were forcibly entering her home in Louisville, Kentucky ; her death sparked extensive protests against racism and police brutality.

08-07.title: The last confirmed lynching of black people in the Northern United States occurs in Marion, Indiana ; two men, Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith, are killed.

01-25.title: Luanda, the capital of Angola, is founded by the Portuguese navigator Paulo Dias de Novais .

03-09.title: Paraguayan forces defeat Manuel Belgrano at the Battle of Tacuarí .

11-17.title: The first known case of COVID-19 is traced to a 55-year-old man who had visited a market in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China.

11-10.title: The 729-foot-long freighter SS Edmund Fitzgerald sinks during a storm on Lake Superior, killing all 29 crew on board.

08-22.title: The District of Columbia Voting Rights Amendment is passed by the U.S. Congress, although it is never ratified by a sufficient number of states.

03-26.title: Spanish Civil War : Nationalists begin their final offensive of the war.

12-12.title: Maria of Enghien sells the lordship of Argos and Nauplia to the Republic of Venice .

02-14.title: The Asbestos Strike begins in Canada. The strike marks the beginning of the Quiet Revolution in Quebec .

11-30.title: In Seattle, United States, demonstrations against a World Trade Organization meeting by anti-globalization protesters catch police unprepared and force the cancellation of opening ceremonies.

04-25.title: The final piece of the Obelisk of Axum is returned to Ethiopia after being stolen by the invading Italian army in 1937 .

04-27.title: World War II: Benito Mussolini is arrested by Italian partisans in Dongo, while attempting escape disguised as a German soldier.

08-16.title: Skookum Jim Mason, George Carmack and Dawson Charlie discover gold in a tributary of the Klondike River in Canada, setting off the Klondike Gold Rush .

10-26.title: Ali Maow Maalin, the last natural case of smallpox, develops a rash in Somalia. The WHO and the CDC consider this date to be the anniversary of the eradication of smallpox, the most spectacular success of vaccination .

10-28.title: NASA successfully launches the Ares I-X mission, the only rocket launch for its short-lived Constellation program .

05-15.title: The UN commemorates the Palestinian Nakba Day for the first time.

02-26.title: Japan and Korea sign the Treaty of Kangwha, which grants Japanese citizens extraterritoriality rights in Korea, opens three Korean ports to Japanese trade, and ends Korea's status as a tributary state of Qing dynasty China.

06-08.title: Downed U.S. Air Force pilot Captain Scott O'Grady is rescued by U.S. Marines in Bosnia .

12-11.title: Glorious Revolution : James II of England, while trying to flee to France, throws the Great Seal of the Realm into the River Thames .

07-30.title: Watergate scandal : U.S. President Richard Nixon releases subpoenaed White House recordings after being ordered to do so by the Supreme Court of the United States .

10-20.title: A KLM Lockheed L-049 Constellation crashes on approach to Glasgow Prestwick Airport, killing 40.

05-26.title: An EA-6B Prowler crashes on the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, killing 14 crewmen and injuring 45 others.

12-24.title: Flying Tiger Line Flight 282 crashes after takeoff from San Francisco International Airport, killing three.

01-01.title: Greece adopts the Euro, becoming the 12th Eurozone country.

06-05.title: The Teton Dam in Idaho, United States, collapses. Eleven people are killed as a result of flooding.

03-12.title: Suharto takes power from Sukarno when the People's Consultative Assembly inaugurate him as Acting President of Indonesia .

05-19.title: Henry I of France marries the Rus' princess, Anne of Kiev .

09-30.title: The Germans commence a counter offensive to retake the Nijmegen salient, this having been captured by the allies during Operation Market Garden .

06-10.title: The Austro-Hungarian battleship SMS Szent István sinks off the Croatian coast after being torpedoed by an Italian MAS motorboat; the event is recorded by camera from a nearby vessel.

04-20.title: Two Austrian army corps in Bavaria are defeated by a First French Empire army led by Napoleon at the Battle of Abensberg on the second day of a four-day campaign that ended in a French victory.

01-06.title: English Restoration : The Fifth Monarchists unsuccessfully attempt to seize control of London, England. The revolt is suppressed after a few days.

11-29.title: LAM Mozambique Airlines 470 crashes in the Bwabata National Park in a pilot mass murder-suicide, killing all 33 people on board.

12-29.title: The launch of HMS Warrior, with her combination of screw propeller, iron hull and iron armour, renders all previous warships obsolete.

05-09.title: The figure who later became Mr. Punch makes his first recorded appearance in England.

08-17.title: A bomb explodes at a wedding in Kabul killing 63 people and leaving 182 injured.

02-06.title: Stephen Harper becomes Prime Minister of Canada .

11-01.title: John Adams becomes the first President of the United States to live in the Executive Mansion (later renamed the White House ).

03-24.title: The McMahon killings take place in Belfast . Six Catholic civilians are shot dead, two others wounded and a female family member assaulted. Police were suspected as being responsible, but no one was prosecuted.

12-28.title: Edward the Confessor 's Romanesque monastic church at Westminster Abbey is consecrated .

01-27.title: The first selections for the National Recording Registry are announced by the Library of Congress .

02-22.title: The Battle of Picotin, between Ferdinand of Majorca and the forces of Matilda of Hainaut, ends in victory for Ferdinand.

12-17.title: The United States and Cuba re-establish diplomatic relations after severing them in 1961.

01-28.title: Elvis Presley makes his first national television appearance.

04-28.title: The Ustaše massacre nearly 200 Serbs in the village of Gudovac, the first massacre of their genocidal campaign against Serbs of the Independent State of Croatia .

06-14.title: Welsh rebel leader Owain Glyndŵr, having declared himself Prince of Wales, allies himself with the French against King Henry IV of England .

03-04.title: Nik Wallenda becomes the first person to walk over the Masaya Volcano in Nicaragua.

01-22.title: The Boeing 747, the world's first " jumbo jet ", enters commercial service for launch customer Pan American Airways with its maiden voyage from New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport to London Heathrow Airport .

01-24.title: Apple Computer places the Macintosh personal computer on sale in the United States.

05-05.title: The World Health Organization declares the end of the COVID-19 pandemic as a global health emergency.

05-03.title: The police force in Birmingham, Alabama switches tactics and responds with violent force to stop the " Birmingham campaign " protesters. Images of the violent suppression are transmitted worldwide, bringing new-found attention to the civil rights movement .

01-09.title: Sriwijaya Air Flight 182 crashes north of Jakarta, Indonesia, killing all 62 people on board.

10-23.title: Spanish Reconquista : At the Battle of Sagrajas, the Almoravids defeats the Castilians, but are unable to take advantage of their victory.

12-25.title: World War I : A series of unofficial truces occur across the Western Front to celebrate Christmas .

05-08.title: Hernando de Soto stops near present-day Walls, Mississippi, and sees the Mississippi River  (then known by the Spanish as Río de Espíritu Santo, the name given to it by Alonso Álvarez de Pineda in 1519).

04-26.title: The Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on mission STS-55 to conduct experiments aboard the Spacelab module.

09-19.title: The state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom is held at Westminster Abbey, London .

04-15.title: At Shaw University in Raleigh, North Carolina, Ella Baker leads a conference that results in the creation of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, one of the principal organizations of the civil rights movement in the 1960s.

09-11.title: Battle of Malplaquet : Great Britain, Netherlands, and Austria fight against France.

03-31.title: An earthquake in Nicaragua destroys Managua ; killing 2,000.

04-09.title: An Embraer EMB 120 Brasilia collides in mid-air with a Cessna 172 over Gadsden, Alabama, killing both of the Cessna's occupants.

06-16.title: World War II : Marshal Henri Philippe Pétain becomes Chief of State of Vichy France ( Chef de l'État Français ).

06-02.title: A collision between two passenger trains and a parked freight train near the city of Balasor, Odisha in eastern India, results in 296 deaths and more than 1,200 people injured.

06-03.title: A Soviet supersonic Tupolev Tu-144 crashes near Goussainville, France, killing 14, the first crash of a supersonic passenger aircraft.

03-14.title: Battle of Mogyoród : Dukes Géza and Ladislaus defeat their cousin Solomon, King of Hungary, forcing him to flee to Hungary's western borderland.

09-10.title: Empress Elisabeth of Austria is assassinated by Luigi Lucheni .

11-26.title: World War II: HMT Rohna is sunk by the Luftwaffe in an air attack in the Mediterranean north of Béjaïa, Algeria .

12-04.title: North Carolina ratifies 13th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, followed soon by Georgia, and U.S. slaves were legally free within two weeks.

08-03.title: Long War : Austria captures Transylvania in the Battle of Goroszló .

05-25.title: The Organisation of African Unity is established in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

09-18.title: Battle of Kapetron between a combined Byzantine-Georgian army and a Seljuq army.

11-22.title: A shooting at a Walmart in Chesapeake, Virginia leaves seven workers dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.

09-02.title: Google launches its Google Chrome web browser.

08-25.title: Ten days after World War II ends with Japan announcing its surrender, armed supporters of the Chinese Communist Party kill U.S. intelligence officer John Birch, regarded by some of the American right as the first victim of the Cold War .

05-11.title: The Istanbul Convention is signed in Istanbul, Turkey .

12-22.title: An ash dike ruptured at a solid waste containment area for a Tennessee Valley Authority coal-fired power plant in Roane County, Tennessee, releasing 4.2 million m 3 (1.1 billion US gal) of coal fly ash slurry in the largest industrial spill in U.S. history.

10-09.title: An Ustashe assassin kills King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and Louis Barthou, Foreign Minister of France, in Marseille.

03-07.title: Lieyu massacre : Taiwanese military massacre of 19 unarmed Vietnamese refugees at Donggang, Lieyu, Kinmen .

02-17.title: Ryan International Airlines Flight 590 crashes during takeoff from Cleveland Hopkins International Airport, killing both pilots, the aircraft's only occupants.

12-26.title: The 6.6 M w Bam earthquake shakes southeastern Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX ( Violent ), leaving more than 26,000 dead and 30,000 injured.

02-02.title: The Detroit Red Wings played in the first outdoor hockey game by any NHL team in an exhibition against the Marquette Branch Prison Pirates in Marquette, Michigan .

11-13.title: The Holland Tunnel opens to traffic as the first Hudson River vehicle tunnel linking New Jersey to New York City.

06-21.title: The Irish village of Knockcroghery was burned by British forces .

02-01.title: Vietnam War : The execution of Viet Cong officer Nguyễn Văn Lém by South Vietnamese National Police Chief Nguyễn Ngọc Loan is recorded on motion picture film, as well as in an iconic still photograph taken by Eddie Adams .

04-18.title: American victory at the battle of Cerro Gordo opens the way for invasion of Mexico.

08-02.title: Edward I of England returns from the Ninth Crusade and is crowned King seventeen days later.

01-12.title: Taal Volcano in the Philippines erupts and kills 39 people.

03-17.title: A plane crash in Cebu, Philippines kills Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay and 24 others.

04-08.title: BOAC Flight 712 catches fire shortly after takeoff. As a result of her actions in the accident, Barbara Jane Harrison is awarded a posthumous George Cross, the only GC awarded to a woman in peacetime.

08-19.title: Tens of thousands of farmed non-native Atlantic salmon are accidentally released into the wild in Washington waters in the 2017 Cypress Island Atlantic salmon pen break .

10-04.title: Otto IV is crowned Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by Pope Innocent III .

10-29.title: United States : Second trial of Sacco and Vanzetti in Boston, Massachusetts .

04-07.title: Two-time Formula One British World Champion Jim Clark dies in an accident during a Formula Two race in Hockenheim .

10-11.title: Cromwell's New Model Army sacks Wexford, killing over 2,000 Irish Confederate troops and 1,500 civilians.

04-14.title: The Pan-American Union is founded by the First International Conference of American States in Washington, D.C.

09-14.title: World War II : The Estonian military boards the Polish submarine ORP Orzeł in Tallinn, sparking a diplomatic incident that the Soviet Union will later use to justify the annexation of Estonia.

12-14.title: The French invasion of Russia comes to an end as the remnants of the Grande Armée are expelled from Russia.

05-28.title: Russo-Japanese War : The Battle of Tsushima ends with the destruction of the Russian Baltic Fleet by Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō and the Imperial Japanese Navy .

11-12.title: Leon Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Communist Party, leaving Joseph Stalin in undisputed control of the Soviet Union .

02-25.title: Soviet NKVD forces in Hungary abduct Béla Kovács —secretary-general of the majority Independent Smallholders' Party —and deport him to the USSR in defiance of Parliament. His arrest is an important turning point in the Communist takeover of Hungary.

07-31.title: Charles Albert of Bavaria invades Upper Austria and Bohemia .

02-12.title: New Zealand's worst maritime disaster of the 20th century happens when the SS Penguin, an inter-island ferry, sinks and explodes at the entrance to Wellington Harbour .

11-08.title: TAAG Angola Airlines Flight 462 crashes after takeoff from Lubango Airport killing all 130 people on board. UNITA claims to have shot down the aircraft, though this is disputed.

09-22.title: Anura Kumara Dissanayake is elected as the 9th President Of Sri Lanka .

05-02.title: The King James Version of the Bible is published for the first time in London, England, by printer Robert Barker.

05-30.title: The Treaty of London is signed, ending the First Balkan War ; Albania becomes an independent nation.

05-13.title: World War II: Yevgeny Khaldei 's photograph Raising a Flag over the Reichstag is published in Ogonyok magazine.

04-12.title: Duke Oldřich of Bohemia deposes and blinds his brother Jaromír, who flees to Poland . [ citation needed ]

08-04.title: American Indian Wars : While protecting a railroad survey party in Montana, the United States 7th Cavalry, under Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer clashes for the first time with the Cheyenne and Lakota people near the Tongue River ; only one man on each side is killed.

06-19.title: Kuwait declares independence from the United Kingdom.

08-13.title: Battle of Mišar during the Serbian Revolution begins. The battle ends two days later with a Serbian victory over the Ottomans.

02-11.title: 2024 Finnish presidential election : Alexander Stubb is elected as the 13th president of Finland .

03-25.title: The Candle demonstration in Bratislava is the first mass demonstration of the 1980s against the communist regime in Czechoslovakia .

08-31.title: The Integral Nationalist Group wins the 1933 Andorran parliamentary election, the first election in Andorra held with universal male suffrage .

03-03.title: World War II : Ten Japanese warplanes raid Broome, Western Australia, killing more than 100 people.

06-15.title: The United States Supreme Court rules in United States v. Álvarez-Machaín that it is permissible for the United States to forcibly extradite suspects in foreign countries and bring them to the United States for trial, without approval from those other countries.

03-22.title: Arthur Leonard Schawlow and Charles Hard Townes receive the first patent for a laser .

01-02.title: Georgia becomes the fourth state to ratify the United States Constitution .

03-19.title: First documented bank heist in U.S. history, when burglars stole $245,000 (1831 values) from the City Bank (now Citibank ) on Wall Street.  Most of the money was recovered.

08-15.title: Will Rogers and Wiley Post are killed after their aircraft develops engine problems during takeoff in Barrow, Alaska .

10-03.title: Project Mercury : US astronaut Wally Schirra, in Sigma 7, is launched from Cape Canaveral for a six-orbit flight.

10-13.title: Ankara becomes the capital of Turkey.

11-11.title: The Turkish parliament passes the Varlık Vergisi,  a capital tax mostly levied on non-Muslim citizens with the unofficial aim to inflict financial ruin on them and end their prominence in the country's economy.

03-11.title: Mikhail Gorbachev is elected to the position of General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, making Gorbachev the USSR's de facto, and last, head of state.

05-06.title: Battle of Prague : A Prussian army fights an Austrian army in Prague during the Seven Years' War .

06-18.title: Aviator Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly in an aircraft across the Atlantic Ocean (she is a passenger; Wilmer Stultz is the pilot and Lou Gordon the mechanic).

03-29.title: The ship Ever Given was dislodged from the Suez Canal .

05-01.title: Portella della Ginestra massacre against May Day celebrations in Sicily by the bandit and separatist leader Salvatore Giuliano where 11 persons are killed and 33 wounded.

04-16.title: India and Bangladesh begin a five-day border conflict, but are unable to resolve the disputes about their border .

09-08.title: World War II: London is hit by a V-2 rocket for the first time.

08-10.title: The Battle of Azaz ends with a humiliating retreat of the Byzantine emperor, Romanos III Argyros, against the Mirdasid rulers of Aleppo . The retreat degenerates into a rout, in which Romanos himself barely escapes capture.

08-28.title: The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 receives royal assent, making the purchase or ownership of slaves illegal in the British Empire with exceptions .

01-05.title: The Daily Mail becomes the first major London newspaper to be published on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean.

05-20.title: Russo-Ukrainian War : Russia claims full control of the Ukrainian city of Mariupol after a nearly three-month siege .

12-10.title: Palestinian minister Ziad Abu Ein is killed after the suppression of a demonstration by Israeli forces in the village ( Turmus'ayya ) in Ramallah .

12-27.title: The Spanish Crown issues the Laws of Burgos, governing the conduct of settlers with regard to native Indians in the New World .

01-10.title: Tashkent Declaration, a peace agreement between India and Pakistan signed that resolved the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 .

11-16.title: The United States and the Soviet Union establish formal diplomatic relations .

09-26.title: The Japanese rail ferry Tōya Maru sinks during a typhoon in the Tsugaru Strait, Japan, killing 1,172.

04-11.title: Battle of the Basque Roads : Admiral Lord Gambier fails to support Captain Lord Cochrane, leading to an incomplete British victory over the French fleet.

05-22.title: South Africa's government approves of racial separation in universities.

05-17.title: American Civil War : During the Vicksburg campaign, Union forces under John A. McClernand defeat a Confederate rearguard and capture around 1,700 men at the Battle of Big Black River Bridge .

09-24.title: The eastern United States is covered by a thick haze from the Chinchaga fire in western Canada.

10-10.title: Ben S. Bernanke, Douglas W. Diamond and Philip H. Dybvig are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences .

12-08.title: U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower delivers his " Atoms for Peace " speech, which leads to an American program to supply equipment and information on nuclear power to schools, hospitals, and research institutions around the world.

02-03.title: Moldavia and Wallachia formally unite to create the Romanian United Principalities .

11-28.title: The Soviet Forces move against Estonia when the 6th Red Rifle Division strikes the border town of Narva, marking the beginning of the Estonian War of Independence .

05-29.title: Albert Einstein 's theory of general relativity is tested (later confirmed) by Arthur Eddington and Andrew Claude de la Cherois Crommelin .

06-17.title: Boxer Rebellion : Western Allied and Japanese forces capture the Taku Forts in Tianjin, China.

12-20.title: A United States Air Force C-124 crashes and burns in Moses Lake, Washington, killing 87 of the 115 people on board.

10-24.title: Arsenal Football Club loses to Manchester United, ending a row of unbeaten matches at 49 matches, which is the record in the Premier League.

03-27.title: World War II: Battle of the Komandorski Islands : In the Aleutian Islands the battle begins when United States Navy forces intercept Japanese attempting to reinforce a garrison at Kiska .

04-13.title: The United States launches Transit 1-B, the world's first satellite navigation system.

01-20.title: The Taula de canvi (Catalan: "Table of change"), described as Europe's first-ever public bank,  began operations inside Barcelona's Llotja de Mar .

12-06.title: Transit of Venus, second and last of the 19th century .

04-04.title: The United States Congress, affirming the Second Continental Congress, adopts the flag of the United States with 13 red and white stripes and one star for each state (20 at that time).

11-06.title: The Kelly Barnes Dam, located above Toccoa Falls College near Toccoa, Georgia, fails, killing 39.

09-05.title: Conscription is made mandatory in France by the Jourdan law .

09-25.title: An explosion of badly degraded propellant charges on board the French battleship Liberté detonates the forward ammunition magazines and destroys the ship.

06-20.title: The experimental MW 18014 V-2 rocket reaches an altitude of 176 km, becoming the first man-made object to reach outer space.

08-01.title: Former US President Donald Trump is indicted for his role in the January 6 United States Capitol attack, his third indictment in 2023.

08-23.title: World War II: King Michael of Romania dismisses the pro- Nazi government of Marshal Antonescu, who is later arrested. Romania switches sides from the Axis to the Allies .

05-12.title: American Civil War: The Battle of Spotsylvania Court House : Union troops assault a Confederate salient known as the "Mule Shoe", with some of the fiercest fighting of the war, much of it hand-to-hand combat, occurring at "the Bloody Angle" on the northwest.

04-01.title: The White Star steamer SS Atlantic sinks off Nova Scotia, killing 547 in one of the worst marine disasters of the 19th century.

10-30.title: Hungarian Revolution : The government of Imre Nagy recognizes newly established revolutionary workers' councils. Army officer Béla Király leads anti-Soviet militias in an attack on the headquarters of the Hungarian Working People's Party .

10-18.title: The Soviet probe Venera 4 reaches Venus and becomes the first spacecraft to measure the atmosphere of another planet.

12-03.title: Mount Marapi located in West Sumatra, Indonesia begins a sporadic series of eruptions . 23 people were killed, and 12 were injured.

10-14.title: Australians vote to reject a constitutional amendment that would have established an Indigenous Voice to Parliament .

09-21.title: American Revolutionary War : Benedict Arnold gives the British the plans to West Point.

12-31.title: The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay, having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to the Spanish.

12-16.title: Hundred Years' War : Henry VI of England is crowned King of France at Notre Dame in Paris.

03-30.title: The Heinkel He 100 fighter sets a world airspeed record of 463 mph (745 km/h).

06-13.title: The USS Jeannette is crushed in an Arctic Ocean ice pack.

10-07.title: Uppsala University is inaugurated after receiving its corporate rights from Pope Sixtus IV in February the same year.

08-11.title: The Great Famine of Europe becomes so dire that even the king of England has difficulties buying bread for himself and his entourage.

10-06.title: Spain's DeSoto expedition takes over the Apalachee capital of Anhaica for their winter quarters.

10-02.title: The "Prelature of the Holy Cross and the Work of God", commonly known as Opus Dei, is founded.

09-07.title: Cardinal Rolando Bandinelli is elected Pope Alexander III, prompting the election of Cardinal Octaviano Monticelli as Antipope Victor IV the same day.

04-02.title: A Soviet bio-warfare laboratory at Sverdlovsk accidentally releases airborne anthrax spores, killing 66 plus an unknown amount of livestock.

12-18.title: The Chicago Bears defeat the Portsmouth Spartans in the first NFL playoff game to win the NFL Championship.

11-09.title: The Committee for Industrial Organization, the precursor to the Congress of Industrial Organizations, is founded in Atlantic City, New Jersey, by eight trade unions belonging to the American Federation of Labor .

05-24.title: Belle de Jour, directed by Luis Buñuel, is released.

09-20.title: Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes tennis match at the Houston Astrodome.

02-24.title: Treaty of Paris between Napoleon and Frederick William III of Prussia against Russia is signed

03-16.title: Mariupol theatre airstrike during the siege of Mariupol .

08-29.title: American Civil War : The Battle of Hatteras Inlet Batteries gives Federal forces control of Pamlico Sound .

03-15.title: Battle of Halmyros : The Catalan Company defeats Walter V, Count of Brienne to take control of the Duchy of Athens, a Crusader state in Greece.

07-28.title: Vietnam War : U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson announces his order to increase the number of United States troops in South Vietnam from 75,000 to 125,000.

08-20.title: World War II : British Prime Minister Winston Churchill makes the fourth of his famous wartime speeches, containing the line " Never was so much owed by so many to so few ".

08-26.title: Exactly 5 years after the 2018 Jacksonville Landing shooting, there is another shooting in Jacksonville, Florida, leaving 3 people dead.

09-15.title: The Soviet ship Poltava heads toward Cuba, one of the events that sets into motion the Cuban Missile Crisis .

08-08.title: Iraq occupies Kuwait and the state is annexed to Iraq. This would lead to the Gulf War shortly afterward.

05-27.title: World War II: In Operation Anthropoid, Reinhard Heydrich is fatally wounded in Prague ; he dies of his injuries eight days later.

10-01.title: A double bombing of an elementary school in Homs, Syria kills over 50 people.

02-13.title: Black college students stage the first of the Nashville sit-ins at three lunch counters in Nashville, Tennessee .

02-29.title: Svend Robinson becomes the first member of the House of Commons of Canada to come out as gay .

02-23.title: Émile Zola is imprisoned in France after writing J'Accuse…!, a letter accusing the French government of antisemitism and wrongfully imprisoning Captain Alfred Dreyfus .

11-07.title: United States presidential election : U.S. President Richard Nixon is re-elected in the largest landslide victory at the time.

01-26.title: The Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory sees first light under the direction of Edwin Hubble, becoming the largest aperture optical telescope (until BTA-6 is built in 1976).

09-04.title: Scotland's Forth Road Bridge near Edinburgh officially opens.

11-02.title: Norman Morrison, a 31-year-old Quaker, sets himself on fire in front of the river entrance to the Pentagon to protest the use of napalm in the Vietnam war.

01-18.title: Frederick I crowns himself King in Prussia in Königsberg .

02-16.title: Howard Carter unseals the burial chamber of Pharaoh Tutankhamun .

12-23.title: The Tampere conference, where Vladimir Lenin and Joseph Stalin meet for the first time, is held in Tampere, Finland .

09-01.title: Six-Day War : The Khartoum Resolution is issued at the Arab Summit, and eight countries adopt the "three 'no's against Israel".
